writeups.title: LIT final - one LIT strategy built from the four 2026 studies
writeups.summary: The four LIT studies (entry, sessions, risk, filters) were merged into one strategy and judged on 2026 only, picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct. The final, LIT final, combines the entry study's CISD entry with a 1-minute confirmation and the risk study's VIX-band target banked at 8R. In 2026 it makes +$38,873 (PF 3.06, 3.1 trades a week, max DD -$3,097), against +$20,487 for the old bot. Almost all of the extra money comes from Jan-Jun, the half the parts were tuned on. In Jul-Oct it makes +$8,212 (PF 2.19), while the old bot made +$15,568 over the same months. It only works on true 1-minute bars, most trades come in the London morning (02:00-08:00 ET), and it has no edge in 2021-25 (PF 1.03). Paper only. Since 2026-10-18 it is the paper bot's strategy (live_model.json, engine/lit_live.py; the old bot runs on as a shadow ledger).

writeups.title: LIT losses - where and why LIT loses in 2026, and the rules worth adding
writeups.summary: Every 2026 trade of LIT final was taken apart (time, level, sweep, inducement, stop, MFE, news, VIX, ES, opens, 1H/4H). 59 stop-outs carry 97% of the lost dollars. They are trades that never worked (median best point +0.3R, 45 minutes to the stop), not shake-outs. About 110 rules were tested, each picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct, plus timeframes and the masters-study filters. Two rules help both halves and the eval: a weekly stop (after 2 stop-outs in a week, half size for the rest of it) and a Monday rule (once Monday has taken Friday's high, only shorts; once it has taken Friday's low, only longs). Together (lit_loss_pack): 2026 +$41.7k, PF 3.66, max DD -$2.3k, eval pass rate 95.5% (was 80%), H1 +$2.1k and H2 +$0.75k better than LIT final. Every exit-management idea (scale-outs, trails, stop to the inducement) and every other timeframe lost money in both halves.

writeups.title: LIT experiments - sizing like a prop trader, a New York session, other targets, other stops, and the masters' ideas
writeups.summary: About 150 variants of LIT final were tested on 2026 CME NQ1! futures (5m + 1m bars). Each was picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct, with 2021-25 as a reference. None of the strategy changes beat LIT final in both halves. That covers a New York second session, 15 target ideas, 5 stop anchors with 4 buffers, breakeven on structure, partials at liquidity, re-entries, minimum 3R and a two-stage entry. The only real gains come from sizing for the MFFU 50K eval. (1) Fast-eval size: $800 risk up to a 40-pt stop instead of 20. It passes about half of all evals within 2 weeks in both halves (H1 52% vs 33%, H2 47% vs 23%) and halves the expected time to a pass, but about 1 eval in 4 fails within 2 weeks. (2) A max-loss room cap: never risk more than 60% of the distance to the trailing max-loss floor. It cuts 2-week failures from 15% to 4% in H1 and leaves H2 unchanged. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT (Liquidity Inducement Theorem) built as its own strategy, head to head with the Liquidity Engine
writeups.summary: Every LIT component the owner listed was built from CME NQ1! 5m data and backtested as a pure LIT strategy (none of the engine's rules). Taken raw, LIT breaks even (PF 0.97 in 2026, 1.01 in 2021-25). The best rule set (strong displacement + deep sweep + previous day/week/month targets) makes money in both periods (2026 PF 1.26, +$5.3k; 2021-25 PF 1.15, +$31.5k) and holds up in every check, but it is far behind the locked bot in 2026 (+$20.5k, PF 3.94). Its 21% losing-trade drawdown makes the MFFU 50K eval fail more often than it passes. Verdict: LIT does not beat the current bot. Five of the owner's components carry a small edge in both periods; the rest do not.

writeups.title: How the LIT and liquidity-inducement traders actually trade, turned into testable rules
writeups.summary: Reimfx's LIT and the closely related "liquidity inducement" school (Marco Trades / Inter Equity Trading, DreamsFX, PhronesisKnight, BornaFX, DTFX), plus ICT's and prop traders' risk rules, read from primary code, student notes, video transcripts and vendor docs. Section 1 is the model in codeable steps (Reim's own box times decoded from his Pine source). Section 2 turns the discretion into rules with parameter ranges. Section 3 covers risk and sizing on the MFFU Builder 50K. Section 4 is one table of ideas with priorities that take into account what the LIT workflow has already tested. No backtests were run for this file.

writeups.title: LIT trade intelligence - every trade with ~60 facts, and what winners and losers have in common
writeups.summary: Every LIT trade (630 backtest trades of the live settings, run lit_live, plus the cloud paper and PC live trades as they come) now carries ~60 facts - 57 known at entry (time, session, ICT macro, swept level type / age / touches, sweep depth, wick, inducements, displacement, CISD wait, stop, R:R, target, VIX / VXN, gamma, ATR regime, Asia / London range, gap, prior day / week, Monday rule, weekly stop, news, size) and 11 outcomes (exit, R, $, MFE / MAE, minutes, time to +1R, heat before breakeven). Each entry fact is split in terciles set on 2026 H1 and checked on H2. 8 of 50 facts point the same way in both halves by 0.1R or more, but shuffled outcomes give 13.4 on average, so as a group the signs are no stronger than chance. The clearest ones are lower VXN, a closer target, a quiet day so far, ES sweeping its own level too, and more than 2.6R of room to the nearest opposing level. Only the last one also leans the same way in 2021-25. Most of these were already tested as rules and none passed. Nothing changes in live_model.json.

writeups.title: LIT performance checks - is live inside the expected range, how robust is the live config, exit efficiency, a monthly walk-forward and a look-ahead audit of every stored run
writeups.summary: Seven read-only checks from the competitor-features list (#6, 7, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14) now run on the live LIT and show on a new Performance page (PC Data > Performance, phone Money > Performance). Expected range - a bootstrap of the 2026 H2 sessions of run lit_live gives the band for N sessions; after 10 sessions the 90% band is -3.7R to +13.0R (median +3.0R) and -$1.8k to +$5.3k on the eval path, 3-8 trades. Robustness of the live config on 2026 (LIT size rule, base +$43,385 PF 4.07) - prices +/-1 tick on every 5m and 1m bar keep 92% of the $ (50 copies, p10-p90 83-100%, all profitable), +/-2 ticks 85%, random 0-3 ticks of slippage on every fill 98%, 10% / 20% of trades missed at random 90% / 80%, a 1-minute late entry 92% (H1 81%, H2 129%), 2 minutes late 68% (H2 37%): a late entry is the weak spot, as batch 3b found for the combo. All stresses together keep 76%. Exit efficiency - 2026 trades kept 48% of all the open profit they saw; the 66 that reached +1R kept 62% of their best move and gave back 1.3R on average (35 ended at breakeven). Walk-forward - re-picking 6 knobs (729 points) every month on all months before made +$29.3k Feb-Oct vs +$33.3k for the fixed live config; it won 3 of 9 months, so keep the config fixed. Look-ahead audit - 499 LIT runs, 1,472 top trades re-built on data cut at the entry bar: 0 changed, 0 flagged (64 runs need a research executor and were skipped).

writeups.title: LIT + retail tools as confluence and size - EMAs, MACD, support / resistance, supply / demand
writeups.summary: The owner asked whether the big retail tools (EMAs, MACD, support / resistance, supply / demand) would make LIT better while keeping about 3 trades a week. This study used them only as a filter or a size change on the 120 trades LIT already takes in 2026 (another study tests them as new entries). 63 retail facts were built, all from bars closed before the entry (look-ahead check 30 of 30 identical). Each was tried 4 ways - skip the trade when the fact is against it, half size when against, x1.25 or x1.5 when with - for 252 tests, scored on the LIT size rule and on the live two_week eval path, picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct 2026. No skip filter keeps 2.9 trades a week (they leave 0.1 to 2.89), and no half-size rule makes more money in both halves. 23 up-size rules pass the letter of the test; all of them are 'bigger size when price is on the trend side of an EMA'. Best: x1.5 when price is on the trade's side of the 1-hour EMA 21, H1 +$42.7k (live +$33.9k), H2 +$11.5k (+$9.5k), eval path 2-week pass H1 63.9% (57.1%), H2 52.2% (unchanged). But they come from more risk, not better picks. Making the same trades bigger at random passes the same test 11-28% of the time and does about as well in Jul-Oct. The 'with' trades beat the 'against' trades in both halves for only 3 of the 63 facts; shuffled facts give 12.3. The eval fails also go up: H1 2-week fails 5.9% to 7.6%, H2 1-month fails 0% to 6.8%. Nothing is adopted, nothing was built, live_model.json is unchanged. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT with bias and discretion - 12 daily-bias methods, an A+ checklist and meta-labeling as size, target or filter
writeups.status: rejected - nothing adopted; one lead (wider target on power-of-3 days) kept as a default-off option for a forward paper check
writeups.summary: The owner said "trading with bias and discretion - there's stuff you haven't tried". 1,842 variants on today's live LIT and on the adopt-candidate combo (t_check + scale_in + be_off), scored on the real MFFU 50K eval path (two_week for 10 sessions, then safe_eval, no reset, $1.90 a micro, true 1m), picked on Jan-Jun 2026 and checked on Jul-Oct. Twelve daily-bias methods were tested, all read before the entry (look-ahead test 8/8): the HTF draw to PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL, the previous day's close, premium/discount, Power of 3 / AMD, the ICT weekly profile, the midnight / 08:30 / 09:30 / 18:00 / weekly opens, the Asia direction, the previous day's displacement, the daily FVG/IFVG, 1H/4H/daily structure, NQ-ES SMT and a vote of five. Each was used as a size tilt, a target tilt and a filter. Size tilts do not work on the eval path (3 of 279 better in both halves): two_week sizes each trade so one winner passes, so a cut costs passes and a size-up hits the caps. Filters drop Jul-Oct below 2.5 trades a week and lose money (0 of 31). The A+ checklist score is not monotonic in Jul-Oct and is backwards in 2021-25. Meta-labeling has no skill out of sample (AUC 0.46-0.52, label-shuffle p 0.47-0.81). One family helps both halves: a farther target on days the bias agrees. Best: on Power-of-3 days (Asia low taken for a long, Asia high for a short), target x1.25 and no 8R bank. On the eval path it makes +$11.3k in H1 and +$3.1k in H2, and 2-week fails fall 9.2 -> 7.6% and 2.9 -> 0.0%. On the combo it makes +$17.2k / +$0.8k. Random trade sets of the same size do as well only 3% of the time. It is not adopted: the H2 gain rests on 4 trades, it was found in a follow-up after both halves had been seen, and on the combo its neighbours (x1.2, x1.3) lose money in H2. Engine option bias_tgt (default off) is ready for a forward paper check. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT risk and money - equity-curve sizing, eval-game refinements, weekly stops, funded risk, and how many evals to run
writeups.status: two adopt-candidates (an eval weekly loss stop at -$1,200, and buying a 2nd eval one week after the 1st); every other idea rejected
writeups.summary: About 300 eval variants (plus 46 funded and 40 portfolio runs) on the exact live LIT trades of 2026, on the real eval path (two_week config C for 10 sessions, then safe_eval, no reset, $1.90 a micro, true 1m), each scored on live LIT and on top of the adopt-candidate combo (t_check + scale_in + be_off), picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct. (1) The old engine's cold-streak filter does not work on LIT - every cold, hot, drawdown and streak rule costs money or raises eval fails in one half. (2) Eval refinements (room share by session, clock press, protect near target, size after a first loss, need buffer, $-to-go caps) change nothing or hurt; after session 10 a 40% safe_eval nudges the eventual pass up but slows it (promising only); start-day rules (weekday, after a LIT loss / win / quiet days, after a cold LIT stretch) do not hold - the cold-stretch rule looks huge in 2026 but rests on 2-4 episodes and reverses in 2021-25. (3) Weekly profit stops cost money; R-based loss stops cut trades below 2 a week or lose passes. One rule holds: once an eval's week is at -$1,200 or worse, no new trade until Monday. 2-week fails 9.2 -> 5.0% (Jan-Jun) with passes unchanged, Jul-Oct pass 50.7 -> 52.2%; neighbours -$700 to -$1,500 all cut fails; 2021-25 fails 5.6 -> 5.2%. It is money-neutral (-$2 / -$3 a month in the portfolio). (4) Funded: LIT's full Kelly is 20-29% of the room; the live funded size already risks about that (max $342-412 a trade), so a ramp after payouts, Kelly fractions, room tiers or streak multipliers add nothing in both halves. (5) MFFU allows 1 sim-funded Builder 50K: buying a 2nd eval 5 sessions after the 1st (while no funded account) pays $662 / $653 a month instead of $641 / $608 and cuts the 6-month no-money risk 9.4 -> 7.4% / 14.8 -> 9.8%. Two evals the same day are the same eval twice. Paper only; nothing live changed (one default-off option added to engine/sizing.py).

writeups.title: LIT market context - dealer gamma, vanna, the VIX term structure, the options calendar and the 0DTE move as size, target or breakeven tilts
writeups.summary: 2,520 context variants were tested on today's live LIT trades and on the adopt-candidate combo (t_check + scale_in + be_off). The context sources were dealer gamma and dark-pool buying (SqueezeMetrics GEX / DIX), vanna proxies (yesterday's VIX and SPX change), the VIX term structure and vol-of-vol (VIX9D, VIX3M, VVIX, SKEW), the 0DTE-implied move (VIX1D / VIX) and the options calendar (OPEX day and week, the week after OPEX, quad witching, VIX expiry, month-end and turn of month). Context was used only as a size tilt, a target / bank change or a breakeven change, never to skip a trade: the trade list is identical in every variant. Judged on the real eval path (two_week for 10 sessions, then safe_eval, no reset, $1.90 a micro, true 1m), pick on H1, check on H2. None passed the strict test: net $ up in both halves, no rise in 2-week fails, neighbouring thresholds holding, more than a handful of trades. 12 of 1,076 size tilts and 73 of 1,444 target / breakeven variants made more money in both halves, about what chance gives; each then failed on more fails, broken neighbours or 1-3 changed trades. The classic dealer-gamma idea (wider target on low gamma, nearer on high gamma) loses $5-17k per half. CBOE put/call is not testable (the free file stops in 2019), and there is no free historical vanna data. Nothing changes in live_model.json.

writeups.title: LIT gap audit - every LIT idea tested so far, what was still untested, and the top 10 untested ideas run on live LIT and on the combo
writeups.status: rejected - nothing new to switch on; the midday profit take is still a small candidate (promising), it improves every eval number except the back-to-back path money
writeups.summary: All 36 LIT write-ups, the report-2 inventory and the 584 LIT runs were read and turned into one table of the ideas already tested (about 130 ideas in 40 study families). 22 LIT / ICT / SMC ideas had never been tested, or never on the real eval path. The top 10 were built as default-off engine options (engine/lit.py) and run as 96 variants, each on live LIT and on the adopt-candidate combo (t_check + scale_in + be_off), 192 runs, picked on Jan-Jun 2026 and checked on Jul-Oct 2026, with money on the real MFFU 50K eval path (two_week sizing, $1.90 a micro). None passes every gate. Killzone-specific settings, ATR stop limits, a maximum sweep depth, Asia-range deviation targets, Monday / 20-day levels (turtle soup), London time exits, re-entry after a breakeven, a 2nd 1m CISD entry, the 09:30 opening model and the failed-zone flip all lose money in a half, raise 2-week fails or rest on a handful of trades. The closest is the midday profit take (out at 12:00 ET when the trade is +0.5R or more): more money at the LIT size in both halves on both bases, a higher 2-week pass rate in both halves, the same fails, more $ per eval, but the back-to-back eval path makes less in H1 (path noise on 7 changed trades). Paper only; live_model.json unchanged.

writeups.title: LIT funded accounts on the new live LIT (t_check + scale-in + BE+1.25) - what to buy, in what order, and what it pays
writeups.summary: The funded-account studies (lit-funded-firms, lit-mffu-rapid-stack, lit-builder-25k, lit-funded-sizing, the payout habit of lit-money-batch2) were re-run on the trades of the new live LIT, with the 15-minute check, one scale-in add after breakeven and breakeven at entry + 1.25 pts all on (630 engine trades, 2026 120, 52 with an add). Every account sizes its adds with the live rule, capped by its own max contracts. Where a best-day rule applies, the adds are trimmed so the day's win stays inside the cap. The current plan (MFFU Builder 50K + LucidPro 50K + FundedNext Rapid Daily 50K, $377 up front) now makes $2,530 a month over 6 months net of every fee on Jul-Oct trades (H2, the number to quote), up from $1,754 on the old trades. Months 4-6 make $3,182. The 6 months lose money in 2.6% of paths, and all three pay $0 in months 4-6 in 5.1%. Each account loses its funded account in 6 months 0.9-1.5% of the time. Adding a Builder 25K one week later adds about $290 a month, and a second LucidPro a week later adds about $840. A Rapid EOD adds about $1,265 a month, but it needs MFFU's written OK, its eval takes about 2 months and the funded news ban costs it a third of the Jul-Oct points. On a cash budget the best order is Builder 50K, LucidPro, FundedNext, LucidPro #2, LucidPro #3, FundedNext #2, each bought when the cash (budget + payouts) allows: $3,280 a month on $300, $4,251 on $600 and $5,090 on $1,000 (H2). On 2021-25 every mix loses money (-$26 to -$144 a month). Paper only; nothing live changed.

writeups.title: LIT batch 3b - ES confirmation, NQ/ES strength, structure breakeven, 10:00 day type, Asia / London range, news days, seasonality, FVG targets, stop-scaled target; robustness and stability of the combo
writeups.status: no adopt-candidate; one promising target idea (fvg extension, live lit only); the combo is robust to slippage and commission, sensitive to a late entry, and sits on a plateau (the 15-min check time is the sharp knob)
writeups.summary: Ten new ideas (about 1,850 variants) were tested as size tilts or management tweaks on today's live LIT and on the adopt-candidate combo (t_check + scale_in + be_off). Scoring used the real eval path (two_week for 10 sessions, then safe_eval, no reset, $1.90 a micro, true 1m). Picked on H1 2026, checked on H2. None passed the strict test on both references. The closest is an FVG target extension: when the VIX-band target sits below an untouched opposite 5m FVG from today or yesterday, aim for the FVG. On live LIT it passes the strict test, holds at its neighbours and changes 6 / 5 trades: eval +$887 / +$7,045, LIT rule +$1,591 / +$1,186. On the combo it gains on the LIT rule (+$1.9k / +$1.8k) but loses -$4.1k on the H1 eval path, so it stays promising, not adopted. ES confirmation is not information: ES takes its matching level within 5 minutes on 88 of 120 trades. Structure breakeven costs $2-32k per half. The 10:00 day read and the stop-scaled target change only 1-6 trades. Robustness: on the LIT size rule the combo keeps 95-96% of its $ at +2 ticks on every fill and 99% at commission +50%. A random 20% of missed fills keeps 81-83%. A 1-minute late entry is the weak spot: H2 falls to 53% on the LIT rule (11% on the eval path), almost all from one trade. Stability: every one-step neighbour of the combo beats live in both halves on the LIT size rule (9 of 11 on the eval path; 550 of 1,215 grid points). The check time of 15 min is the one sharp knob. A walk-forward (3-month pick, next month) does not beat the fixed pick: +$35.1k vs +$36.1k on the LIT rule, Apr-Oct.

writeups.title: LIT batch 3a - ICT macros, volume, delta, sweep rejection, speed, level age / touches, equal highs-lows, round numbers, level type, consecutive-day sweeps
writeups.summary: 13 setup-quality ideas were tested on today's live LIT trades and on the adopt-candidate combo (t_check + scale_in + be_off), as size tilts, fitted size weights, filters (only if 2026 keeps >= 2.5 trades/week) and, for equal highs/lows, as extra LIT levels. About 1,800 variants, judged on the real MFFU 50K eval path (two_week for 10 sessions, then safe_eval, no reset, $1.90 a micro, true 1m), pick on H1 (Jan-Jun 2026), check on H2 (Jul-Oct 16). None passed the strict test (net $ up in both halves, no rise in 2-week fails, neighbours hold, enough trades, beats flat leverage), on either reference. The best money idea, a 1.5x size when the fill lands within 10 minutes of an ICT macro window, adds +$7.1k / +$2.3k on live LIT but loses -$8.8k in H1 on top of the combo, loses in 2021-25 and nudges the Monte Carlo fail rate up. Round numbers (a swept level within ~8 pts of a 00/50 handle, 1.5x) add money in H1, H2 AND 2021-25 under the LIT size rule and beat flat leverage there, but lose on the eval path; it is noted for a future funded sizing only. Equal highs/lows are already LIT levels (build-ups): removing them costs -$14k in H1, looser or tighter detectors lose; today's detector stays. Filters all cost money and most drop below 2.5 trades/week. Nothing changes in live_model.json.

writeups.title: MFFU Builder 25K next to the 50K - the 25K's rules, its eval sizing and copy trading both accounts with one LIT bot
writeups.summary: The owner is buying an MFFU Builder 25K ($63) to trade with the same LIT signals as the Builder 50K eval, with each account sized on its own room. Rules were re-checked on 2026-10-19 ($1,500 target, $1,000 EOD trailing max loss locking at +$100, $600 soft daily loss, 20 micros, no eval consistency rule, 1 min day, news allowed; the $600 daily loss is in the current guide, an older "legacy" 25K page says none). The 50K's config C scaled to the 25K passes 55% / 51% of evals within 2 weeks (H1 / H2), as fast as the 50K, and hardly ever fails outright. Its weak spot is different. About 12-16% of 25K evals end up "stuck": the room falls under $100, and even 1 micro on a 40-80 pt LIT stop would breach it, so the bot stops trading. The pick (H1) is 50% of the room instead of 60%, and safe_eval at 30% after session 10. It passes 54% / 48% in 2 weeks, 79% / 77% in the end (Monte Carlo), and is dead (failed or stuck) in 10 sessions 11% / 4%. That is $117-132 per 2-week pass and about $80 per eventual pass at $63, against $174-181 and $115-119 on the 50K. Copy trading on the same day is close to one bet: when one account passes, the other almost always does too (correlation 0.92-0.95). Both pass in 2 weeks about 50% of the time, and both die about 7-10% (MC H1 / H2 6.8 / 6.4%). Starting the 25K one week later decouples them: at least one passes in its own 2 weeks 68-76% of the time instead of 55%, and both die only 2-3%. Funded 50K + 25K at the H2 rate is about $1,015 a month of payouts, or $780 a month net over the first 6 months including fees and the eval time. Copying between your own MFFU accounts is reported as allowed by third parties. MFFU's own fair-play page only forbids copying that "coordinates trades for an unfair advantage" and copying other people, so ask support in writing. The live code cannot run a 25K yet, because live.py sizes every account on the 50K's plan. Paper only; nothing live was changed.

writeups.title: LIT on stacked MFFU Rapid / Rapid EOD 50K accounts next to the Builder 50K
writeups.summary: The owner asked whether to stack MFFU Rapid EOD accounts. Rules were searched again on 2026-10-19 and every Rapid account was played on the exact live LIT trades of 2026, with the real Tier-1 news calendar applied to the funded accounts. Both Rapid evals break the 2-week eval rule, and no sizing fixes it. The 50% best-day rule needs 3 winning days and the 30% rule needs 4; LIT makes about 0.8 winners a week. Best p10 is 9.4% (Jan-Jun) / 6.4% (Jul-Oct) for Rapid and 0% for Rapid EOD; the median pass takes 22-27 and 41-43 sessions. The news rule costs much less than feared. Only 5 of the 120 2026 trades are open at a Tier-1 release (not 25), but one of them was a big CPI-day winner, so funded Jul-Oct drops from $1,345 to $1,078 a month (Rapid) and from $1,607 to $1,291 (Rapid EOD). Rapid EOD is the better of the two: it loses a funded account in 6 months 9-12% of the time, against 16-22% for Rapid. Stacking scales the money and the shared risk together, because copies bought the same day are the same account N times. Builder + 2 Rapid EOD makes $1,879 a month on Jul-Oct for $280 up front (Lucid + FundedNext plan: $1,754, $377). Builder + 1 Rapid EOD + Lucid + FundedNext makes $2,413 a month and spreads firm risk. All of it loses money on 2021-25. Held until MFFU answers in writing. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT on 3 funded accounts - which 2 to add next to the MFFU Builder 50K, how to size each, and what it pays a month
writeups.summary: Rules were re-checked on 2026-10-19 for the firms whose rules let this bot run (bots allowed, NinjaTrader available, the same bot allowed at other firms). Each plan was played end to end on the exact live LIT trades of 2026 with an eval sizing and a funded sizing tuned to that plan's rules on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct. Recommended: keep the MFFU Builder 50K and add a LucidPro 50K and a FundedNext Rapid Daily 50K. Over 6 months from the purchase, net of every fee, the three pay on average $2,315 a month on Jan-Jun 2026 trades and $1,754 on Jul-Oct (months 4-6, once all three are funded, $2,944 / $2,373). The accounts trade the same signals, so their results are 84-91% correlated. In about 1 path in 8 (Jul-Oct) all three pay nothing in months 4-6. Losing all three funded accounts is rare (0.1%), because the funded sizing shrinks with the room. On 2021-25 (reference) every plan and every combination loses money. A Tradeify account is ruled out because Tradeify bans running the same bot at another firm. Apex, Take Profit Trader, Alpha and Elite ban full automation or NinjaTrader. MFFU Rapid models the most money but is held back for now, for two reasons: MFFU has not said a Rapid can sit next to a Builder 50K, and its funded news ban could cut it to a quarter (77% of LIT's 2026 points come from trades open at 08:30 ET). Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT new entries and confluences - MSNR levels, inducement into order blocks, stacked confluence, confluence as size
writeups.status: inducement-count size (option idm_size) is a candidate for the lit size rule / funded only - on the eval path (two_week) it is rejected; every new entry type rejected
writeups.summary: The owner asked for more LIT entry types and confluences (MSNR, IDM, build-ups, 15m order blocks, smart money trap, stacked setups) and 3+ trades a week. 362 variants on the exact live LIT, picked on Jan-Jun 2026 and checked on Jul-Oct 2026, scored in $ at the LIT size and on the MFFU 50K 2-week eval under the live two_week sizing. No new entry type adds money in both halves next to today's LIT. MSNR 15m support/resistance setups make money on their own (H1 PF 4.19 +$23.7k, H2 PF 2.65 +$8.6k), but most of them are the same days and moves as today's trades: added as a 2nd trade a day they cost $1.6k in Jan-Jun and push the Jul-Oct 2-week fails from 2.9% to 10.1%. SMC inducement into a 15m/1h order block gives 13 trades in 2026 and loses in Jan-Jun. Stacked confluence (2+ of OB, SMT, MSNR, 2+ inducements, build-up, major level, 4h storyline) on setups the live filters reject adds +$3.3k / +$0.6k but doubles the Jul-Oct 2-week fails. One sizing rule holds: trades whose sweep took 2+ inducements (within 2 ATR, 48 bars) earn 1.0-1.2 R against 0.0-0.2 R for the rest in Jan-Jun, Jul-Oct and 2021-25; 1.5x on those and 0.75x on the rest (risk capped at $990) makes H1 +$40.2k (vs +$32.5k) and H2 +$12.7k (vs +$8.9k), 2-week fails 9.2 -> 6.7% and 2.9 -> 0.0%, but drawdown is about 30% bigger. Paper only. On the real eval path (two_week 10 sessions then safe_eval, $1.90, true 1m; engine/sizing.py now applies the multiplier) it does not hold: H1 net -$0.5k, 2-week fails 9.2 -> 10.1%, H2 2-week pass 50.7 -> 49.3%, and on top of t_check + scale_in + be_off it costs $12.9k in H1. For the eval keep it off; the best eval combination stays t_check + scale_in + be_off.

writeups.title: LIT more setups a week - ES/MES, 15m/30m/1h setups, missed fills, looser filters, higher-tier 2nd trades
writeups.summary: The owner said there must be more LIT setups a week. 95 variants on the exact live LIT (1m entries, live stops and VIX-band targets, Monday rule, weekly stop, $1.90 a micro), scored in $ at the LIT size and on the MFFU 50K 2-week pass rate under the live eval sizing (two_week for 10 sessions, then safe_eval), picked on Jan-Jun 2026 and checked on Jul-Oct. None passes. ES traded as MES loses money in Jan-Jun (PF 0.75, -$4.5k) and NQ+ES together fails 17-29% of evals in 2 weeks. 15m setups add 2-6 trades a half and lift the 2-week pass rate in both halves (Jan-Jun 52.9% -> 63.0%, Jul-Oct 50.7% -> 52.2%), but cost $322 in Jan-Jun and raise Jul-Oct fails 2.9% -> 7.2%. 1h setups never fit the 80-pt stop (0 trades). Re-arming missed fills, longer limits and looser filters all lose in at least one half. The extra setups exist, but they fall on days that already traded, have stops over 80 pts, or are weaker. Today's LIT stays.

writeups.title: LIT money batch 2 - minis for commission, a second scale-in add, 15m eval booster, profit lock, London/NY tilt, funded compounding, payout policy
writeups.status: one small adopt-candidate (wait until $1,500+ is above the buffer before asking for a funded payout); minis are real but tiny; everything else rejected
writeups.summary: Seven money ideas, judged by the LIT rule (2026 only, pick on Jan-Jun, check on Jul-Oct; live sizing two_week for 10 sessions then safe_eval, no reset, $1.90 a micro, true 1m fills). (1) NQ minis instead of 10 micros save $14.32 a mini (MFFU NQ ~$4.68 round turn, unconfirmed), but only 13 / 2 eval-path trades reach 10 micros, so ~$36 / $12 a month: real, tiny, needs NQ routing. (2) A second scale-in add gains in H1 but loses $17.8k in H2 vs one add; rejected. Side finding: scored with the true worst open price, the scale_in candidate's H1 2-week fails are 7.6%, not 10.1% (live 9.2%). (3) 15m setups only in eval sessions 1-10 at half size cut 2-week fails (9.2 to 7.6, 2.9 to 1.4) for +$617 / +$165, but rest on 4 / 1 trades; rejected as too thin. (4) Funded compounding: no gain in either half. (5) Payout policy: asking only once $1,500+ is available pays +$175 / +$189 per account in 6 months (+$29 / +$32 a month) and loses fewer accounts (1.0 to 0.8%, 1.5 to 1.4%); neighbours agree; taking the $500 minimum each time pays 71% less. (6) Stepped profit locks lose H1 money in every version. (7) London vs New York size tilts: the sign flips between halves; rejected. Paper only; nothing live changed.

writeups.title: LIT big ideas - scale-in after breakeven, a trend-day mode, volatility sizing, news-release setups
writeups.status: one adopt-candidate (scale-in on a 1m cisd after breakeven, with the stop moved to the add); trend-day mode and volatility sizing rejected; news-release setups not testable
writeups.summary: Four ideas never tested on LIT were scored by the LIT rule (2026 only, pick on Jan-Jun, check on Jul-Oct; adopt only if both halves gain net $ AND MFFU 50K 2-week passes under the live sizing, two_week then safe_eval, $1.90, true 1m fills, stop before target in a bar). (1) Scale-in passes. After breakeven, wait for the first 1m pullback of at least 0.25R, then a 1m CISD close back up, and add the same number of micros at the next 1m open. The add uses the same breakeven stop and the same target, and its open risk is never above the first entry's $ risk, 60% of the room or the soft daily loss left. Once the add is +1 of its own risk, the whole position's stop moves to the add's price. Results: H1 net +$36,723 to +$49,205, H2 +$9,674 to +$26,015, 2-week pass 52.9 to 53.8 (H1) and 50.7 to 52.2 (H2), H2 fails unchanged at 2.9, H1 fails 9.2 to 10.1. Every neighbour holds in both halves (pullback 0.1-0.4R, add 0.75-1.5x, add fills up to 2 pts worse). The control (stop move with no add) does not. But the pass-rate gain is one eval start per half, and in H2 it rests on one trade, so the money is solid and the pass rate is thin. Starting at half size and adding at +1R cuts 2-week fails to 4.2 / 0.0%, but H1 loses $4.2k: rejected. (2) Trend-day mode: 0 of 16 H1-fitted classifiers held in H2. (3) Volatility tilts: 0 of 160 better in both halves. (4) News-release sweeps need a 94-395 pt stop: 0 trades in 2026 and in 2021-25. Engine option scale_in (default off; backtest only, the live route cannot send an add yet). Paper only.

writeups.title: Owner's LIT notes (screenshots from the owner's LIT study group, 2026-10-18)
writeups.summary: Paraphrased rules to test. LIT only; judged on 2026 (pick Jan-Jun, check Jul-Oct).

writeups.title: LIT untested target and exit ideas - HTF FVG / order block targets, news and midday exits, reverse-inducement exits, a daily profit stop, other bank levels
writeups.status: one small adopt-candidate (take the profit at 12:00 et when the trade is at least +0.5r); everything else rejected
writeups.summary: 58 variants of the live LIT trade were tested on CME NQ1! futures (5m + true 1m bars, 2026), each picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct, with the live eval sizing ($800 up to a 25-pt stop, 60% room cap). Same setups, same entries, same stops; only the target or the exit changes. Higher-timeframe targets (the nearest unfilled 1H/4H fair value gap or order block) lose money in both halves, alone or next to the VIX band. Taking profit before 08:30 news, leaving when the reverse trade's inducement gets taken, a second trade a day with a daily profit stop, banking at 6R/10R/never, a VIX band x 0.8/1.2 and front-running the band are all rejected. One idea helps both halves a little - take the profit at 12:00 ET (the end of the New York morning) when the trade is at least +0.5R, else let it run: H1 +$915 (PF 4.01 to 4.09), H2 +$1,132 (PF 2.51 to 2.68), 2021-25 reference +$13.6k, same 2.6-3.1 trades a week, 2-week eval pass H1 37.5% to 39.8%. It touches only 7 trades of 2026, so it is a small, thin edge. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT untested stop ideas - close-based stops, stops behind the next liquidity, ATR buffers, time-based breakeven, profit locks
writeups.summary: Five stop ideas nobody had tested on LIT yet (plus two extra ones) were run on the exact live LIT signals with the live eval sizing, 44 variants in all. Each was picked on Jan-Jun 2026 and checked on Jul-Oct 2026. None made more money in both halves, so nothing changes in the bot. The live stop (1 tick past the sweep extreme, closed on a touch, breakeven at +1R) stays. LIT stop-outs are real: 52-53 of the 53 stop-outs in 2026 also closed a 1m candle past the stop, so waiting for a close only loses more. A wider stop behind the next swing or equal lows only buys a smaller size. A later breakeven turns scratches into full losses. A profit lock at 75-85% of the way almost never fires (1-3 trades in 2026); at 50-60% it cuts the runners. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT untested entry ideas - buy-stop entry, chasing a missed limit, ES SMT, and a LIT opening model
writeups.summary: Four entry ideas nobody had tested on LIT were run on the exact live LIT signals with the live eval sizing, 33 variants, picked on Jan-Jun 2026 and checked on Jul-Oct 2026. Three are rejected - a buy-stop above the 1m CISD candle (H2 -$4.8k), chasing a missed limit on a 1m pullback (H1 -$4.6k), and ES SMT as a size boost, a filter or an early 1m trigger (H2 -$0.6k to -$11.6k). One passes the rule, barely - the LIT opening model on the overnight high/low (a 09:30-10:00 sweep of the 18:00-09:30 range, inducement taken first, 1m CISD, entry by 10:00 as an extra setup on days the bot has not traded yet). It adds +$1,589 in Jan-Jun and +$839 in Jul-Oct at 3.4 / 3.0 trades a week and keeps the eval pass rate about the same (91% / 95% vs 92% / 96%). It rests on only 13 trades in 2026 (3 winners), and letting the entry run to 10:15 instead of 10:00 turns Jan-Jun negative (-$4.0k), so it is a small, fragile adopt-candidate - default off, paper shadow first. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT untested bias and regime ideas - VIX regime size, target-aware eval size, weekly profile, Asia range gate, event days
writeups.status: rejected - nothing adopted (vix >= 20 upsizing is a neutral "can't check yet")
writeups.summary: 39 variants of five bias / regime ideas were tested on the live LIT trades (CME NQ1! 5m + true 1m bars, 2026), each picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct, at the live eval sizing ($800 up to a 25-pt stop, 60% room cap). Same setups, entries, stops and targets; only which setups are taken or the size changes. None is adopted. Upsizing when the prior VIX close is 20 or more (x1.5) adds +$5.3k in H1 and +$1.4k in 2021-25, but Jul-Oct 2026 had one VIX day >= 20 and no trade on it, so it cannot be checked out of sample (NEUTRAL). The weekly-profile skip (Thu/Fri, no trade toward a week high or low made Tue-Wed) looks better in both halves on the eval path (+$2.7k / +$0.8k), but at a fixed size it loses $2.1k in H1 (it skips a +$2.4k winner) and the H1 pass rate falls from 92% to 85%: rejected. Target-aware eval sizing, the Asia range gate, OPEX / month-end / quarter-end days and VIX < 15 downsizing are rejected. Big-tech earnings days could not be tested (no earnings dates in data/news/events.csv). Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT two-week eval - how to pass the MFFU 50K in 10 sessions or less
writeups.summary: The owner's order is that an MFFU eval must pass within 2 weeks (10 sessions), so the eval mode was rebuilt for that one number, using the exact live LIT trades (same signals, same 1m entries, same stops). The new idea is "one winner passes" sizing. Each trade is sized so that, if it reaches its target, it covers what is still missing to +$3,000. The caps are the room to the max-loss floor, the $1,000 soft daily loss and 40 micros. Fixed $ schemes, a clock press, profit protection, more LIT shots a day, an earlier window and start-timing rules were tested next to it. Today's eval mode passes 40% of Jan-Jun starts and 25% of Jul-Oct starts within 10 sessions (cost per 2-week pass $228 / $373). The recommended config (one winner passes, all the room, weekly stop on) passes 58% / 54% (Monte Carlo 51% / 57%), so a 2-week pass costs $158-171 at $91.80. The price is that 18-22% of evals fail within 2 weeks instead of 0-3%. A safer option (60% of the room, no weekly stop) passes 53% / 51% with only 3-8% failing ($174-181). No config gets past about 55-59%. LIT's ceiling is about 70%: that is the share of 10-session windows where at least one target is hit and a perfect hindsight sizing could pass. More LIT shots and an earlier window do not help. Start timing is not proven. Paper only; nothing live was changed.

writeups.title: LIT trade selection - can we pick and size LIT setups like an experienced trader?
writeups.summary: Every LIT setup of 2026 was collected (330 setups on 167 days, 176 that would have filled if taken alone, against the 120 the bot takes) with 50 features known at the decision moment (look-ahead test passed). Person-like rules (an A/B/C grade, wait for a better setup, size by grade) and a small walk-forward model were scored on the real one-trade-a-day path at the eval size ($800 up to 25 pts, 60% room cap). The model has no skill out of sample (test AUC 0.23-0.52), and the data-mined grade only works on the half it was picked on. Two simple size tilts help both halves a little. (1) Fresh trap: 1.25x when the inducement swing is at most 6 bars (30 min) old, else 0.75x. H1 +$6.4k, H2 +$0.9k, max DD lower in both halves, 2-week eval pass H1 43.0% vs 37.5%. (2) The trader's A/B/C grade, A 1.5x / C 0.5x: H1 +$1.4k, H2 +$1.6k, 2-week pass H2 34.6% vs 29.5%. Each passes a shuffle test in one half only, and 2021-25 is worse for both, so neither is proven. Skipping setups ("wait") never pays: a later setup rarely comes. Win rate cannot be raised without dropping below 2 trades a week. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT tight stops and bigger size - do we need 50-60 point stops, and what if we trade more micros or 1 NQ?
writeups.summary: On the exact live LIT signals (120 trades in 2026), 48 stop and entry variants were tested, each at 12 sizes, with the MFFU 50K eval simulated. Tighter stops do not help. The 1m protected-swing stop (median 14-17 pts instead of 44-52) looks great in Jan-Jun only because the size rule then risks about 2.7 times more money. At the same $ a trade it wins Jan-Jun and loses Jul-Oct: winners win less often (23% to 13%) because many turn into breakeven scratches, and 2021-25 loses money. Skipping wide stops leaves 0.1-1.2 trades a week. Limit entries on the 1m retest miss the best winners. The speed has to come from size on the live sweep-extreme stop, with a cap that never risks more than 60% of the room to the max-loss floor. $800 up to a 40-pt stop + that cap passes 47% of evals within 2 weeks in both halves (live 29% / 23%), with 5% failing within 2 weeks. $800 up to a 25-pt stop + the cap keeps the live pass rate (92% / 96%) and passes faster (2-week pass 37.5% / 29.5%). 1 NQ fixed fails 28-38% of evals within 2 weeks. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT stops, targets and management (lit_A entry fixed), tuned on 2026 only
writeups.summary: With lit_A's entry fixed, the target decides almost everything. Aiming at the edge of the VIX one-day band (18:00 open ± 1 implied move) instead of PDH/PWH/PMH turns 2026 H1 from −$4.4k into a profit and holds on H2. With a 1-tick stop buffer, stops up to 100 pts, a 4R fallback, exits walked on 1m bars, and no bank (or a bank at 8R), 2026 makes +$36.4k (PF 2.71) or +$23.5k (PF 2.10) with a max drawdown of −$3.2k at 3.4 trades a week. Both halves are profitable and every neighbour is profitable. The no-bank version leans on one +18.7R trade (14 April). In 2021-25 the drawdown is −$24k (reference only).

writeups.title: LIT spec, part 1: sessions, timing, opens, PO3, high/low of week, NWOG/NDOG, VIX move, bias
writeups.summary: What public LIT / ICT / TTrades / "liquidity inducement" sources say about session boxes, opens, PO3, the weekly window, opening gaps, the VIX move and daily bias, turned into codeable rules with parameter ranges. Tune on Jan-Jun 2026, check on Jul-Oct 2026; 2021-25 is a reference line only.

writeups.title: LIT sessions and timing - which boxes, windows, opens and day rules make LIT pay in 2026
writeups.summary: Restricting the swept liquidity to four session boxes (Asia 20:00-00:00, London 03:00-04:00, NY 08:00-09:00, NY 08:00-08:30) plus the previous day/week/month highs and lows turns lit_A from PF 1.26 (+$5.3k, losing in Jan-Jun) into PF 2.14 (+$11.8k, DD -$2.4k) in 2026, better in both halves. Adding the Mon-Wed range rule on Thursday/Friday gives PF 2.37 (+$12.7k, DD -$1.9k) at 1.99 trades/week. Opens/PO3, bias, one-direction and 2-trades-a-day rules did not help.

writeups.title: LIT report tests - every codable rule of the owner's LIT Complete Report, tested on 2026
writeups.summary: The owner's LIT Complete Report (29 chapters) was read end to end and every rule a computer can follow was listed against what LIT live already does. Most of them were already in LIT or had been tested before. The 16 rule ideas that were new became 44 variants, tested on 2026 CME NQ futures (5m + 1m), each picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct. None improves both halves in a way that holds up. The closest, skipping a setup when another level sits within 0.5R of the entry, adds $1,313 in H1 and $10 in H2, but at 0.4R or 0.6R it loses money in H2, so it is noise. The report's own example model (chapter 21) made no trade at all in 2026. LIT live stays as it is (2026 +$41,734, PF 3.66; H2 +$8,962). Chapters 27-28 led to four execution fixes - cancel-pending entries, partial exit fills, CME early closes and a frozen paper ledger - all with tests. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT report coverage - is everything in the owner's LIT Complete Report in the bot or tested?
writeups.summary: The owner's LIT Complete Report was split into 436 items (definitions, rules, numbers, times, checklists, skip reasons, variants, execution and clock requirements, glossary, worked examples, chapter 26 audit facts). 260 are in the bot (50 of them partly), 67 were tested and rejected, 7 were tested as evidence or are neutral, 22 are missing, and 80 are context only. A second pass tested the 38 variants the first pass had not run (strength tiers, range premium/discount, time and news exits, stop buffers, equal-level tolerance, round numbers, mean threshold, DST London box, execution stress). None improves both 2026 halves, so LIT live stays as it is - 2026 +$41,734, PF 3.66, 2.91 trades a week; H2 +$8,962 (about $2,400 a month). The missing items are mostly undefined models in the report and live-data chores, the biggest being the contract roll in the live window.

writeups.title: LIT playbook - the model as the bot trades it, the report's checklists, reasons to skip and glossary
writeups.summary: A beginner's guide to LIT as the paper bot trades it today (live_model.json, run lit_live), built from the owner's LIT Complete Report (29 chapters). It gives the 10 steps of a trade, the report's before/after-trade checklists and its reasons to skip, each marked with whether the bot applies it, what cancels a setup, the session clocks, a short glossary and what the report's audit of published LIT trades found. Main lessons from the report - a sweep alone is not a signal, a checklist is not a probability, and no published LIT record proves a profitable NQ strategy - are all things the bot's tests already respect. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT order blocks - finding them like a LIT/ICT trader, and every way to trade them with LIT
writeups.summary: A new order-block detector (engine/lit_ob.py, no look-ahead, checked on 20 charts) finds the last opposite candles before a displacement that breaks structure and leaves a fair value gap, on 5m, 15m, 1H, 4H and daily candles, with mitigation, breakers, extreme vs decisional blocks and the owner's mitigation rules. It was put into the live LIT trade in every role - point of interest, entry, target, obstacle, and as a source of new trades (sweep into or inside a fresh 1H/4H/daily block, also as a second trade a day) - and scored with both live sizes (eval and two_week), picked on Jan-Jun 2026 and checked on Jul-Oct 2026. Nothing improves both halves, so nothing goes live. The reason is simple: only 10-25 of the 120 live trades sweep into a fresh higher-timeframe block, those trades are not better than the rest in Jan-Jun, and fresh HTF blocks that LIT could trade on its own add 1-16 trades a year. Two ideas are worth watching: skipping trades with a fresh opposing 15m/1H block less than 2R away halves the 2-week eval fails (H1 8.4% to 3.4%, H2 2.9% to 0%) but costs about $4.5k-6k in Jan-Jun and does not raise Monte Carlo passes; HTF block setups as a second trade a day add about 10 trades and a little money in both halves but leave the Jul-Oct 2-week pass flat (50.7% to 49.3%). Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT on the 1-minute chart - smarter entries and "this trade is wrong" exits, tested like a person would trade them
writeups.summary: The owner asked for 1-minute entries and loss management that thinks like a person. On the exact live LIT signals (2026, true 1m bars, eval sizing $800 up to a 25-pt stop + the 60% room cap), 153 variants were tested, picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct. 1m entry filters (inner 1m inducement, 1m displacement, volume, absorption, patience, pullback entries) all lose money in both halves. The classic "trade is wrong" signals (1m CISD against, a new 1m low, back inside the swept level, higher low taken, a volume surge against) do cut 50-100% of the losers early, but they also kill 30-80% of the winners. In Jul-Oct the winners dip as deep as the losers before they run (median 0.54R against), so every one of these signals loses money there. One signal is real in both halves: ES not confirming. When ES closes a 5m bar beyond its own sweep extreme and NQ then prints a 1m CISD against, before the trade has reached +0.75R, exit at the next 1m open. It cut 8 of 53 losers at about half a loss and touched no winner: H1 +$446, H2 +$1,514. That is small and rests on 8 trades. Profit rules (structure trail, closing at the 18:00 or midnight open on a stall, skipping breakeven on fast moves) do not hold in both halves. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT on every prop firm - which account, which size, and what a Monday start on the MFFU 25K Builder or Rapid looks like
writeups.summary: The current rules of 60 futures prop-firm plans (MyFundedFutures Builder, Rapid, Rapid EOD and Pro; Topstep, Apex, Tradeify, Lucid, Take Profit Trader, Alpha Futures, FundedNext, Bulenox; every size) were run on the exact live LIT trades of 2026 with the eval sizing scaled to each plan's max loss. One rule decides almost everything for LIT: a best-day consistency rule in the eval. Plans without one (MFFU Builder, Lucid Pro, Tradeify Growth, FundedNext Rapid, Bulenox, Apex, Alpha Zero) pass 24-48% of evals within 2 weeks; plans with one (MFFU Rapid 50%, Rapid EOD 30%, Topstep 55%, Take Profit Trader, LucidFlex, Tradeify Select, FundedNext Legacy, Alpha Standard) pass 0-7%. A Monday start on the MFFU 25K Builder passed 34% of 2026 Monday starts within 2 weeks (H2 27%) but failed 17% within a month and 37% in the end, because 1 micro on a 60-88 point stop is too big for a $1,000 max loss; the 50K Builder passes at the same speed and fails 5% within a month (H2 0%). The MFFU Rapid passes 5% within 2 weeks at any size. Top picks for LIT: MFFU Builder 50K (keep), Lucid Pro 50K, FundedNext Rapid Daily. Paper only; rules read through search results on 2026-10-18 and partly unconfirmed.

writeups.title: LIT loss learning - the 15-minute check, and what the losses can't tell us
writeups.summary: Every 2026 LIT trade was re-played on its true 1-minute path and scored on the number that matters most, the MFFU 50K 2-week pass rate under the live two-week sizing (config C). One rule holds in both halves. The 15-minute check: 15 minutes after the fill, if the trade has never been +0.5R in profit and the 1m close is more than 0.3R below the entry, get out at the next 1m open. It cut 13 trades in 2026, all of them would-be full stop-outs, at about -0.45R instead of -1R, and touched no winner. 2-week pass H1 52.9% -> 57.1% and H2 50.7% -> 52.2%; 2-week fails 8.4% -> 5.9% and 2.9% -> 0%; the Monte Carlo agrees in both halves; eval-path money +$4.4k (H1) and +$5.0k (H2). Its neighbours (0.25-0.4R, +0.3-0.7R, minute 15-20) agree. Checking earlier (5-12 min) or later (25-30 min), or keeping the check on after minute 15, kills slow winners in Jul-Oct. Everything else failed: wider stops (stop-outs are not stop hunts), tightening the stop with time, scratching after a small profit, sequence memory (after a loss in the same direction, the same level type or the day before), and a walk-forward context model (no skill out of sample). Small sample (13 trades), so it is an adopt-candidate for after the launch, not before.

writeups.title: LIT live fills - how the orders really fill on the MFFU account, and what that does to the numbers
writeups.summary: A study of how LIT's orders fill on NinjaTrader -> Tradovate -> CME for the MFFU account, and a realistic fill model built from it (engine/lit.py option "fills", off by default). No backtest matches live exactly, so this is the most realistic model we can defend, plus a tool (tools/fill_audit.py) that measures the real fills. Order handling costs little. MFFU's $1.90 commission, stop slippage, the spread, the tick-rounded target limit and the breakeven lag together cost about $1.2k of 2026's $41.7k under the LIT size rule (+$40.5k, PF 3.48 instead of 3.66). H2 is unchanged at about $2,400-2,500 a month. The real problem is timing. The PC bot sees the entry only after the 1m bar after the CISD has closed, then waits for its next 60-second poll, so it buys about 95 s late. The entry lands anywhere from 9 points better to 25 points worse (sd 7.5 pts) and can risk up to 1.65 times the planned amount. On the eval sizing the bots trade, that drops the 2026 pass rate from 85% to 71% and 1-month passes from 55% to 50%. With two small code fixes (decide on the CISD bar's close, poll 2 s after each minute) the entry is 6 s late, the error is 0.6 pts and the eval odds are back to the backtest's (pass rate 85%, 2 weeks 34.5% / 2.4%). Keep stop-market stops and the target where it is. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT learning loop - how the bot learns from its losses, what it may change, and what it would have learned in 2026
writeups.summary: Every finished LIT trade now goes into a journal (data/lit_journal.jsonl) with its 50 entry facts, the outcome, MFE/MAE and a loss cause code. Every Sunday a review re-estimates a small set of bounded size knobs (0.5x to 1.25x per bucket, a skip only for a bucket that lost money over 15+ trades) with shrinkage toward 1.0x. Each proposed change has to pass six guardrails before it can go live, and every decision is logged and can be reverted. Replayed on 2026 with only the data before each Sunday, the learner made 3 changes, all on the inducement (trap) age, by late April: stale traps 0.5x, fresh traps 1.25x. That is the same thing the trade-selection study found by hand. It made 0 changes on 2021-25. The money was not better in both halves. H1 eval path +$3.6k but funded -$1.1k; H2 -$0.4k, and 2-week passes fell from 29.5% to 23.1%. So the loop ships in OBSERVE mode. It journals, learns and logs what it would do, and leaves the size alone. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT launch audit - is anything missing for day trading? (2026-10-18)
writeups.summary: End-to-end launch check of the LIT bot before the 18:00 ET Sunday open. Real MFFU eval at 21:00 ET - go only after the five checks in section 0 (Sim101 round trip on the Surface first; the code itself is sound). Paper - ready tonight. Needs the contract-roll fix before Wed 2026-12-09, and the cloud heartbeat alert moved to the London session this week. Fixed today - Windows Update restart hours and the PC wake time (both were set for the old 08:00 strategy, while LIT trades from 02:00). Calendar, DST, holidays, early closes and the Sunday open are handled. A news blackout would change 1 of 120 trades in 2026 (H1 +$207, H2 $0), so no news rule.

writeups.title: LIT higher-time-frame confluences - draw on liquidity, dealing ranges, PO3, bias, structure, HTF FVGs and time of week, deep dive
writeups.summary: The owner asked for a deep dive into higher-time-frame (HTF) context. Every 2026 LIT setup (330 setups, 176 that would fill alone, 120 taken) got 42 causal HTF facts, read as 49 HTF confluences (1H, 4H, daily and weekly candles built from the CME NQ1! 5m file; look-ahead test 30 of 30 identical) plus 26 LIT facts. 75 confluences were scored in Jan-Jun (pick) and Jul-Oct (check), with permutation p-values and a multiple-testing correction. Nothing survives the correction, and the number that "hold in both halves" (18 of 65) is exactly what chance gives (17.7). The owner's main idea, trading WITH the HTF draw, flips between the halves and loses money as a filter, as a London-only filter and as a size rule. 86,000 2- and 3-way combinations were tried: the HTF-only ones picked on Jan-Jun held in Jul-Oct 0 times out of 22. Skipping setups never works (below 2 trades a week). Three small size tilts help both halves and are adopt-candidates at low confidence. (1) The 4H draw, size-neutral: 1.4x when the nearest unswept 4H swing is on the target side, else 0.8x. It is the only rule that raises the 2-week pass in both halves (H1 37.5% -> 42.2%, H2 29.5% -> 34.6%; cost per 2-week pass $245 -> $218 and $311 -> $265), but Jul-Oct 1-month fails go from 0% to 10.3%. (2) The fresh trap times a clear HTF path: H1 2-week pass 52.3%, H2 unchanged at 29.5%, +$10.3k / +$1.5k. (3) A clear 1H path (no opposing 1H FVG before the target): H1 41.4%, H2 unchanged, +$6.6k / +$0.4k. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT funded sizing - how big to trade once the MFFU eval is passed
writeups.summary: After the MFFU Builder 50K eval passes, the goal changes from speed to payouts without losing the account. The exact live LIT trades of 2026 were replayed on a modelled MFFU funded account (EOD trailing $2,000 locking at +$100, $1,000 soft daily loss, payouts above a $2,100 buffer, $500-$2,000 a request, best day at most 50% of the cycle, 5 sim payouts, 80% split). Keeping today's normal or eval size on a funded account loses 20-22% (Jan-Jun) / 28-29% (Jul-Oct) of accounts within 6 months. The new mode "funded" risks 40% of the room to the floor (at most $800, so a fresh account trades the normal LIT size), sizes so a winner pays at most $1,500 (the 50% best-day payout rule), keeps the weekly stop, and skips a trade when even 1 micro could reach the floor. It loses 1.0% / 1.5% of accounts in 6 months and pays $4,613 / $4,433 in 6 months ($769 / $739 a month) vs $3,423 / $3,020 for normal size ($1.90 commission). The best-day cap is the lever that matters; fixed $ tiers, fractional Kelly and % of the room all sit on the same plateau once it is on. Paper only; live_model.json is unchanged.

writeups.title: LIT filters and confluences on top of lit_A, judged on 2026 only
writeups.summary: lit_A loses money in 2026 H1 (PF 0.70, -$4.4k) and makes it all in H2 (PF 2.63, +$9.7k). Of 86 filter/confluence variants, two LIT ideas lift PF in BOTH 2026 halves: trade only from the discount side of the New Week Opening Gap (longs below its midpoint, shorts above) and half size outside the high/low-of-week window. Together 2026 PF 1.26 -> 2.13, +$5.3k -> +$9.9k, max DD -$6.9k -> -$3.4k, at 2.0 trades/week. Displacement, sweep depth, vector candles, VIX move, SMT with ES, news and volatility regime did not hold in both halves.

writeups.title: LIT execution spec (inducement, sweep, displacement, vectors, structure shift, entry, stop, target, management)
writeups.summary: Codeable LIT execution rules gathered from public sources (Reimfx's own "LIT - Timing" Pine code, Reim's 2020 WWA call notes, TTrades pages, LIT/SMC indicator docs, one third-party LIT bot spec), mapped onto engine/lit.py with parameter ranges. Tune on Jan-Jun 2026, check on Jul-Oct 2026; 2021-25 is a reference line only.

writeups.title: LIT entry precision - can the entry be "on the dot"? Direct limit vs confirmation vs refined limit, per original setup
writeups.summary: The owner asked for entries that are on the dot. 43 entry variants were run on the exact live LIT setups of 2026 (true 1m bars, costs in), picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct, scored in $ on the LIT rule and on the MFFU 50K 2-week pass rate under the live two_week sizing. Following the owner's advanced report (ch.5 / ch.13 experiment 1), every entry rule was also compared per original setup, with a missed fill counted as $0, at one common $1,000 budget. Today's entry (tap of the 5m CISD level, then the first 1m CISD, buy the next 1m open) is still the best. No variant is better in both halves. A plain resting limit at the zone fills 3 setups in 4 instead of 1 in 2 and gets a better price on the trades both take, but the extra fills are the setups that never confirm, and they lose (H1 -$28.9k at $1,000 a setup). Every refined limit misses the runaways; every later or slower confirmation (1m BOS, 2m/3m CISD, close back above the zone) gives up more than it saves. The closest miss, a limit at the CISD candle close for 1 minute then market, is +$1.3k in H1 and -$0.2k in H2 (2-week pass 52.9 / 49.3 vs 52.9 / 50.7). Nothing to implement. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT entry models (inducement, structure shift, entry type, 1m precision), tuned on 2026 only
writeups.summary: With lit_A's sessions, levels and targets fixed, the way the trade is entered decides whether LIT works in 2026. A 5m CISD structure shift, a pre-sweep inducement (I-a), and a 1m CISD confirmation after price taps the CISD level lift 2026 from PF 1.26 / +$5.3k to PF 2.18 / +$20.5k with a max drawdown of -$2.7k at 3.0 trades a week. It was picked on Jan-Jun 2026 and stays profitable on Jul-Oct 2026 (PF 1.71). It does not hold in 2021-25 (PF 1.01, reference only).

writeups.title: LIT all hours - trading the whole CME day (Asia, 15:30-16:00, more trades a day, re-arming, the 18:00 F-BoS, trendline liquidity)
writeups.summary: The owner asked for LIT to look for trades all the time (CME NQ trades 18:00-17:00 ET). 30 variants on the exact live LIT (1m entries, live stops and targets, two_week eval sizing, costs in), picked on Jan-Jun 2026 and checked on Jul-Oct. Nothing passes both halves. Adding the Asia session (18:00-02:00) to the one daily slot gives more money in Jul-Oct but less in Jan-Jun (-$5.5k) and fewer 2-week eval passes in Jan-Jun; Asia setups on their own lose money in Jan-Jun (PF 0.82). Two trades a day, one per session and re-arming after a target or breakeven all trade more (3.4-5.6 a week) and make more in Jul-Oct, but every one loses money or 2-week passes in Jan-Jun and most raise the eval fail rate. The 15:30-16:00 extension changes nothing (2 trades). The owner's F-BoS idea (a false break of the 16:30-17:00 build-up at the 18:00 open) is the closest: +$107 in Jan-Jun, +$4.8k in Jul-Oct, Jul-Oct 2-week passes 50.7% -> 66.7%, but Jan-Jun passes stay 52.9% with fails 8.4% -> 13.4%, and its 16 trades in 2026 have 3 winners (none in Jan-Jun; one +$3.6k trade carries Jul-Oct). Trendline/channel liquidity as an extra level is worse in both halves. The live LIT (02:00-15:30, 1 trade a day) stays. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT advanced report ch2-4 - thesis boundary, session carryover, weak reactions, ES same event, owner's session and inducement notes
writeups.summary: The owner's LIT Advanced Decisions Report (chapters 2-4, experiment 4 of chapter 13) and his LIT group's session / Smart Money Trap / inducement notes became 176 variants on the 2026 LIT path, each picked on Jan-Jun and checked on Jul-Oct, under the live two-week eval sizing. Nothing is adopted. Four variants improve both halves; three are lone points whose neighbours fail, and the best one (skip a sweep made by one huge 5m bar with no pause before it) changes only 2 trades per half. The session rules (Asia direction carries into London, London into NY, no inducement before NY) and the Smart Money Trap (untaken liquidity right beside the zone) all cost money or eval passes in at least one half. Carrying Asia theses into the 02:00 order window helps Jul-Oct and hurts Jan-Jun. LIT live stays as it is. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT advanced report ch.7 audit (clocks, bar edges, unresolved records) and experiment 5 (NQ/ES divergence at the same event)
writeups.summary: The owner's LIT Advanced Decisions Report asks whether clocks, candle edges and missing data bend the backtest. On the 120 LIT trades of 2026 they barely do. With 1m bars the entry is at a bar's open, so no stop or breakeven exit shares a bar with the target. Every fixable item together (a stop bar that opened through the stop, 50 missing 1m minutes in 9 trades, the 15:55 flat clock, the early-close holidays) moves 2026 by about -$500 of +$41,734, mostly in H1. The real distortion is in the eval scoring. Starts near the end of a span cannot see 10 or 20 sessions, which inflates H2's quoted 2-week pass rate at the LIT size (23.1% vs 17.4% on full windows; 1 month 44.9% vs 32.2%). runlib now has a switch for that, off by default. Experiment 5 (NQ takes a level while ES holds its same-time copy, or the reverse), used as a size multiplier and judged under the live two_week sizing, is rejected. The divergence trades are not better, and the two rules that gain in both halves (+$350 / +$430-510) do worse than sizing up random trades. Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT advanced management - breakeven versus recoveries, partials at the first obstacle, target choice by location and deadline, and a target that trades before the fill
writeups.status: one small adopt-candidate (breakeven stop at entry + costs); everything else rejected or not testable
writeups.summary: The owner's LIT Advanced Decisions Report (chapters 6, 8, 9, 10 and experiments 2-3 of chapter 13) was tested on the exact live LIT trades of 2026 (true 1m bars, live sizing two_week for 10 sessions then safe_eval, $1.90 commission, no reset), each idea alone and on top of the 15-minute early-loss check (t_check). Breakeven at 1R stays. It removes about 1 recovery for every 7 full losses it saves (H1 3 of 29 breakeven trades would have gone on to the target; H2 0 of 5), which is below the 13% break-even recovery rate, and without it 2-week fails jump (H1 9.2% to 13.4%, H2 2.9% to 7.2%). Moving the breakeven later (1.5R, 2R), to structure (a new 1m/5m swing, price leaving the mitigation area) or holding it while the zone's 50% is untouched does not hold in both halves. Partials at the first obstacle cost a lot, because LIT's sizing needs the whole target to pass the eval with one winner (2-week pass H1 52.9% to 22-50%). Nearer targets from the entry location, the day's range or a time deadline help H1 only. A target that trades before the fill happened once in 2026: not testable. The one change that helps both halves is small and mechanical. Put the breakeven stop at entry + 1.25 pts (5 ticks = $1.90 commission + 1 tick of exit slippage) instead of at the entry. It changed no exit in 2026, and each breakeven exit then nets about $0 instead of about -$2.40 a micro. H1 +$681, H2 +$80 on the eval path, 2-week pass unchanged (52.9 / 50.7), H1 2-week fails 9.2% to 8.4%. With the 15-minute check: H1 +$928, H2 +$20, H1 fails 6.7% to 5.9%. Engine option be_off (default 0 = today). Paper only.

writeups.title: LIT Complete Report - item-by-item inventory against the bot
writeups.summary: All 436 items of the owner's LIT_Complete_Report.docx (29 chapters, 28 tables, 8 figures), each with its status in the LIT bot - 210 in the bot, 50 partly, 67 tested and rejected, 5 tested as evidence, 2 neutral, 22 missing, 80 context only. Test results in research/writeups/lit-report-coverage.md.

writeups.title: LIT Advanced Decisions Report (report 2) - item-by-item inventory against the bot

writeups.title: Retail strategies on their own (EMA, MACD, support/resistance incl. ORB, supply/demand) - which versions make money on NQ
writeups.summary: The owner asked whether EMA, MACD, support/resistance and supply/demand strategies make money on their own, separate from LIT. 13,320 versions (8,636 with different trades) were tested as standalone NQ strategies on real CME NQ1! 5m data, with costs ($1.40 a micro + 1 tick slippage), structural stops, picked on 2021-11..2024-12 and checked untouched on 2025 and 2026. Three families have versions that made money in all three periods. The best robust ones: S/R bounce at the prior-day / overnight high and low (+$40.3k / +$36.1k / +$6.1k at $500 risk a trade, PF 1.20 / 1.79 / 1.16), the 8/21 EMA opening-hour momentum (+$37.9k / +$23.8k / +$5.4k, PF 1.11 / 1.25 / 1.07) and the 15m EMA ribbon (+$41.6k / +$12.6k / +$2.5k). PD/ON break-and-retest with a limit at the level is the strongest in 2026 (PF 3.13, +$21.2k) but was flat in 2025. MACD versions picked in-sample are flat to negative in 2026. Supply/demand loses in almost every version. All edges are thin next to LIT (2026 PF 1.1-1.2 vs 4.07), 2026 H2 is negative for most, and the eval odds are far worse than LIT's. Correlation with LIT is low (-0.1 to +0.26). Worth paper-trading the PD/ON bounce and the opening-hour EMA as a second-account idea; not worth real money yet.

writeups.title: What other trading bots and trader tools do better than ours - 40 features compared, the 15 worth building, and what not to copy
writeups.summary: A web scan (2025-2026 sources) of bridges (TradersPost, PickMyTrade, CrossTrade), platforms (NinjaTrader, Tradovate, TradeStation, Sierra Chart, QuantConnect / LEAN), retail AI and bot apps (Composer, Capitalise.ai, Trade Ideas Holly, TrendSpider, 3Commas, Cryptohopper, Collective2), prop-firm copiers and risk lockers (Replikanto, Tradovate Group Trade, Tradesyncer), journals (TradeZella, Tradervue, TraderSync, Edgewonk), alerting and status tools (PagerDuty, healthchecks, Upptime) and open-source bots (freqtrade, Jesse, Hummingbot, Nautilus Trader). Our bot already has more than most of them for a one-strategy prop trader: a backtest that matches the live loop, Monte Carlo eval odds, a fill audit, guards, an eval lifecycle, recap cards, trade intel and business tools. It is weaker in four areas. (1) It does not warn before a trade: there is no push when a setup arms, and nothing logs that the owner was present, which MFFU requires. (2) Alerts never escalate: a critical alert is sent once, cannot be acknowledged and has no levels. (3) Nothing checks the cloud monitor itself, or that the PC and the cloud run the same rules. (4) Nothing says whether live results are still inside the range the backtest expects. The ranked top 15 are mostly small (S) changes to engine/push.py, engine/ops_checks.py, engine/live.py and the phone app. Paid bridges and copiers, cloud order routing, auto re-optimisation, DCA / grid / trailing exits and plain-English AI strategy builders should not be copied.
