writeups.title: Win rate and more trades: new windows, second trades, partials, entries, filters
writeups.summary: More trades from new windows or second trades lose money in 2021-25 every time (London, Asia, pre-open, lunch, late PM, 2 a day), even at a quarter size. The things that raise the win rate (partials, a depth limit, HTF filters) earn less money or cut trades below 2 a week. One small change helps both periods with every trade kept: half size when the sweep ran 3.5+ ATR past the pool (2026 +$293, PF 3.94 to 4.11; 2021-25 +$1.5k, PF 1.27 to 1.32, max drawdown -$9.3k to -$7.5k, 1-month eval fails 5.2% to 3.5%).

writeups.title: MFFU rulebook (Builder 50K / 25K) and does the bot follow it
writeups.summary: Every MyFundedFutures Builder rule that matters for the bot, from MFFU's own help center (searched 2026-10-18), and a check of the bot against each one (tests/test_mffu_rules.py, 43 ok, 0 fail, 5 warnings). The bot breaks no rule. Five gaps to fix. (1) MFFU charges $1.90 per micro round trip, not the $1.40 the backtests use: about -$310 to -$350 a year. (2) The 7-day inactivity rule: LIT went 7+ days without a trade 3 times in 2026, and nothing warns you. (3) If MFFU wants 2 trading days to pass, the bot stops trading once the target is hit, so you must place one small trade the next day yourself. (4) After a pass, switch the sizing to funded by hand. (5) A full stop-out can reach $1,008 against the $1,000 soft daily loss. That is a pause, not a fail.

writeups.title: What to expect: streaks, drawdowns, flat months and the odds inside a 2-week eval
writeups.summary: The locked strategy wins 1 trade in 4-5 and loses or scratches the rest, so long runs without a winner are normal: 33 trades in a row without a win happened once (Sep-Nov 2025, -$3,126), and 2026 had 16 (Apr-May, -$1,667). A loss does not make the next trade worse (after a loss +0.02R, after a win -0.01R in 2021-25, p=0.79), so sitting out or halving the trade after a max-size loss loses money in both periods (rejected). Most months lose a little (median month -$184 over 5 years, 40% of months positive; 2026 median +$1,162, 50% positive); 13 trades made the whole 5-year profit. In a 2-week eval expect 4+ non-winners in a row in about half of the starts (2021-25 58%, 2026 27%), a $1,000 dip in 12% (2026 1%), a $2,000 dip in 1%.

writeups.title: VWAP and volume profile as confluence
writeups.summary: None of 24 VWAP and volume-profile ideas made the live strategy better in both 2026 and 2021-25 when used to size trades up or down (every trade still taken, 2.2 and 3.2 trades a week). The only raw pass, 1.25x size on days that open inside yesterday's value area (2026 PF 3.50 vs 3.48, 2021-25 PF 1.10 vs 1.09), fails the robustness checks, so the live strategy stays as it is.

writeups.title: Unexpected factors: 33 things the owner would not think of, none of them real
writeups.summary: 33 unusual conditions knowable at entry (VIX / VXN / GEX / dark-pool buying, overnight and gap size, inside days, days since a 2% day, trades already this week, pre-market sweeps, sweep-to-trigger time, zone and candle sizes, relative volume, pool count, month-to-date P&L and more) were ranked on 2021-25. The best one, "the sweep extreme was made before 09:30" (125 trades, +0.159R vs -0.022R), has a t of 1.3 and a shuffle test says a random relabelling beats it 16% of the time alone and 95% of the time once you allow for 33 tries. The 1.25x size rules that "beat the baseline in both periods" do so only because they add leverage: flat 1.25x on every trade makes more (2021-25 +$18,350 vs +$17,472-17,919). Nothing to adopt.

writeups.title: Trade construction: what to change before Sunday
writeups.summary: One change is worth making, together with the sizing change: on trending days move the stop to breakeven at +3R instead of +1R. With the sizing change it adds +$4.8k to 2021-25 (PF 1.19 → 1.27) and changes nothing in 2026 evals; on today's sizing alone it causes extra late-May 2026 eval fails, so then keep the current rules. Stops, targets, the other exits, filters and timing are already at their best; 120+ variants tested, no leak found.

writeups.title: The eval game: which plan, when to start, two accounts, after a fail, and the road to the first payout
writeups.summary: The MFFU Builder 50K is the right eval for this strategy (1.24 evals per pass in 2026, 2.52 in 2021-25, about $313 / $1,006 of fees per funded account); the $1.5k add-on fails twice as often, plans with a best-day rule in the eval take 2-17 months, and the best moment to start is right after the cold-streak filter switches back to full size (2021-25 pass within a month 26% vs 9% overall, 2% in a cold streak). A second account on the same trades buys no speed, after a fail the next pass takes a median 3.3 months, and once funded the first payout takes 3.3 (2026) / 7.7 (2021-25) months if MFFU's 50% best-day rule applies at payout (1.3 / 1.7 months if not) while 21% / 58% of funded accounts hit the trailing loss before any payout.

writeups.title: Targets: where profits are taken
writeups.summary: Today's target (nearest major pool at least 1.5R away, banking at 5R when the draw is farther) is the best of 15 variants. Nearer caps (3-4R) cut 2026 profit by $5-8k; farther caps (6-8R) help 2021-25 a little but cost 2026 $5-7k; exiting in front of the pool changes almost nothing.

writeups.title: Stress tests of the locked strategy: costs, price feed, worst start, size rounding, contract caps, late fills
writeups.summary: The locked strategy survives 2-tick slippage or doubled commission (2021-25 still +$13-14k, PF 1.21-1.22) but 3 ticks plus doubled commission takes 58% of its 2021-25 profit (+$6.9k, PF 1.11), and about half of every cost hit comes from the cold-streak filter flipping state on 3-26 trades. TradingView (MNQ1!) and the Python bot (NQ1!) will end a year roughly $5k apart with no bias; the fastest way to fail an eval is 7-8 full-size losers right after a good run (6-8 sessions, Feb 2023 and Nov 2024); 47% of trades are 1 micro and cost about $450 a year; a 20-micro cap costs 17% of the profit, a 10-micro cap 39%; filling one bar late loses about half of 2021-25.

writeups.title: Stops: where the stop should go
writeups.summary: Today's stop (2 points beyond the sweep extreme, 10-60 points) is the best of 19 variants. Wider buffers, volatility-scaled (ATR) buffers, other min/max limits and stops beyond the gap all lose money in 2026, 2021-25 or both; no stop change is recommended.

writeups.title: Risk summary: size down the two kinds of trades that lose
writeups.summary: Recommendation: quarter size (not half) in cold streaks and half size on late entries. Same trades: 2021-25 +$11.5k instead of +$6.5k (PF 1.19 vs 1.09, max DD -$9.2k vs -$11.4k), 2026 +$20.6k instead of +$20.1k (PF 4.12 vs 3.48), 1-month eval fails in 2021-25 9.4% to 5.1%. For the 2-week eval rule, an optional fast mode ($800 on any stop until the eval is $1,000 down) doubles eval speed at the same evals per pass but fails more evals a year.

writeups.title: Risk and sizing: every sizing idea tested on both periods
writeups.summary: Changing how much the bot risks per trade moves money and drawdown together and does not fix 2021-25. More risk ($1,000-1,200, or no wide-stop scaling) makes more in 2026 but doubles eval fails; less risk drops below 2 setups a week. The changes that help both periods size down specific losing trades: quarter size in cold streaks, half size on late entries.

writeups.title: Parameter robustness: does the lock sit on a plateau or on a peak?
writeups.summary: Mostly a plateau, with one ridge. Cold size, late size, the trending-day breakeven (anything from +3R to never gives the same money), the $ risk and the wide-stop rule all move smoothly. The exception is the cold-streak lookback of 15 signals: 15 and 16 give +$16.4k / +$16.9k in 2021-25, but 14 gives +$13.3k, 13 gives +$7.8k and 17 gives +$10.7k, so about half of the 5-year gain over the morning rules (+$6.5k) depends on that one number. Every one of 105 neighbouring combinations stays profitable in both periods (2021-25 worst +$6.8k, 2026 worst +$19.6k). The lock has 17 of 55 rolling 6-month windows negative (morning rules 22) and a longest flat stretch of 68 weeks (85).

writeups.title: Moving averages as confluence
writeups.summary: The textbook "trade with the EMA trend" filters all cost money (2026 net falls by $5-8k). The one moving-average fact that helps is a warning sign: when price is 3+ hourly ATRs on the wrong side of the 1-hour EMA 20 (a "falling knife"), trading at half size lifts 2021-25 from +$6.5k to +$9.6k (+$127 to +$189 a month, PF 1.09 to 1.13, 1-month eval fails 9.4% to 6.2%) while 2026 is unchanged (+$20.1k, PF 3.49), with every setup still traded.

writeups.title: Monte Carlo of the MFFU 50K eval: how often, how fast, how many evals
writeups.summary: One 50K eval on the locked strategy has about a 35% chance of passing within 60 sessions, 30% of failing and 35% of still running (the real history says 41 / 22 / 37); a typical pass takes 28 sessions, and a funded account costs 1.9 evals and about 5.5 months of fees (roughly $840 at list price), median 15 weeks. Starting the eval during a cold streak cuts the 1-month pass odds from 22% to 4%, so time the purchase to the filter. The fast press gets funded in a median 9.8 weeks for 3.7 months of fees but fails half of its evals.

writeups.title: Managing the trade: breakeven, locks, time stop, giveback
writeups.summary: Today's management is at its sweet spot on all-days rules, with one exception: on trending days (10-day efficiency above 0.45) waiting until +3R to move to breakeven adds +$4.7k to 2021-25 (PF 1.09 → 1.15) and leaves 2026 net unchanged (+$20.1k). On today's sizing it adds some late-May 2026 eval fails (beyond 1 month); with the sizing research's quarter size in cold streaks it is clean (+$4.8k in 2021-25). Profit locks, other time stops and giveback levels all lose.

writeups.title: Loss anatomy: where the money leaks
writeups.summary: In 2021-25 the losses gave back 92% of what the winners made (285R won, 287R lost). The leaks are long cold streaks, not big single losses (the worst day is -$875). Full stop-outs are 80% of the money lost, and trades taken in a cold streak lost money in both periods.

writeups.title: Leakage check: does the backtest peek at the future?
writeups.summary: No leak. Switching off the trade memory (memory_seed) and the exit learner (exit_learn) gives exactly the same 768 trades as the live strategy, so every result in this research is leak-free as it stands.

writeups.title: Intraday anatomy: when, how and where the bot's trades make or lose money
writeups.summary: The clock does not decide the trade (every hour and weekday flips between 2026 and 2021-25); what the trade is made of does. CISD triggers beat IFVG triggers in both periods (2026 PF 5.7 vs 2.4, 2021-25 PF 1.53 vs 1.11), 30-40 pt stops and equal-highs/lows targets lose money in both. Halving the 30-40 pt stops is the one clean small win (2026 +$413, 2021-25 +$115, max drawdown -$9.3k to -$8.1k, 1-month eval fails 5.2% to 4.0%); adding CISD x1.25 and half size on equal-highs targets makes 2026 +$3.7k and 2021-25 +$1.4k with less drawdown in both, but it is three in-sample slices stacked, so it needs a critic before Sunday.

writeups.title: Eval sizing: can the eval's own state pass more MFFU evals?
writeups.summary: Sizing from the eval's state (cushion above the trailing max loss, profit, distance to the target) cuts eval fails a lot (2021-25 1-month fails 9.4% to 0.3-2%), but it also passes fewer evals a year and leaves 43-60% of evals stuck after 3 months, and the result depends on the exact threshold. None beats fixed sizing robustly; the recommended cold-streak / late-entry sizing improves evals more (2.63 evals bought per pass in 2021-25 vs 3.89). For the owner's 2-week rule see the fast mode in risk-summary.md.

writeups.title: Cutting losses to pass more MFFU evals: what works, and how high the pass rate can go
writeups.summary: No loss-cut rule makes a big, proven difference. The best new idea, half size for the rest of the eval week after two losing trades in that week, lifts the pass rate of decided evals from 40% to 42% (2021-25) and 53% to 56% (5 years), makes a little more money in both periods (2026 +$289, 2021-25 +$828) and cuts 2021-25 1-month fails from 5.2% to 3.1%. Its neighbours agree, but the trades it shrinks are not worse than average, so it is a small safety rule, not an edge. The intraday package does not survive the critic: CISD x1.25 lowers the pass rate, and the 30-40 pt and equal-highs slices flip by year or by odd/even month. The math: with a 21% win rate, a +$542 average win and a -$114 average loss, 2021-25 passes about 40% of decided evals at today's size. 70-80% is only reachable in a 2026-like market (91% today), or by trading so small that one eval takes 6-12 months.

writeups.title: Cross-market and regime context: does the market around the setup matter?
writeups.summary: Mostly no. VIX level and change, the VXN/VIX ratio, dealer gamma (GEX), NQ-vs-ES relative strength, SMT divergence and the shape of the entry day do not split trades in a way that holds in both 2026 and 2021-25; 25 of 32 size rules were rejected. One small thing does hold: when BOTH the 10-day and the 20-day trend reading say "trending" (12 trades in 2026, 75 in 2021-25), the reversal loses money in every period; half size there adds +$378 in 2026 (PF 3.94 to 4.16, drawdown -$2,249 to -$1,871) and +$677 in 2021-25 (PF 1.27 to 1.29). The bigger lead is that the 20-day trend test picks the bad days better than the live 10-day test (swap: 2026 +$2.1k, 2021-25 +$5.6k, but more 1-month eval fails); it needs an engine option and a longer live data window before it can be tested exactly.

writeups.title: Calendar and seasonality: does the date matter?
writeups.summary: No. Across 36 calendar factors (weekday, month, month turn, holidays, OPEX, FOMC/CPI/NFP days, DST and roll weeks, first trade of the week) nothing holds in both 2026 and 2021-25 beyond what chance produces. The only rule that is better in both periods, half size the day after NFP, gains $748 over 5 years and $256 in 2026 on 3 trades; a random group of the same size does as well 15% of the time. Keep trading every day at the normal size.

writeups.title: Bias, filters and timing: which trades to take, and how big
writeups.summary: Two simple biases separate trades in both periods: fading yesterday's candle and trading on the side of last week's midpoint. As filters or score points they cut trades below 2 a week and the replacement trades lose; as a size-down (70% size when both disagree) they raise PF in both periods (2026 3.48 → 3.62, 2021-25 1.09 → 1.12) and cut 2021-25 drawdown, for −$0.75k in 2026. No filter or timing change beats today's rules.

brain_help.levels: The map: every liquidity level LIT watches today (session boxes, previous day / week / month highs and lows, opening gaps, equal highs / lows).
brain_help.sweep: Price trades through a level (takes the stops resting there) by at least 0.5 ATR.
brain_help.inducement: Before the sweep, a smaller swing near the level was taken first: early traders trapped (within 1 ATR of the level, at most 36 bars old).
brain_help.displacement: A strong candle back the other way: body at least 0.8 ATR.
brain_help.cisd5: Change in state of delivery: a 5-minute close back through the open of the last run of candles into the sweep extreme. This is the setup.
brain_help.limit: A limit order at the CISD level, valid 30 minutes (6 bars of 5m).
brain_help.cisd1m: Once the limit is tapped, the bot waits up to 20 one-minute bars for a 1-minute CISD to confirm.
brain_help.entry: Entry at the next 1-minute open, routed about 3 s after the 1m CISD close.
brain_help.trade: Managing: breakeven at +1R, the 15-minute check, the VIX-band target (banked at 8R), flat at 15:55.
brain_help.done: One trade a day, or the 02:00-15:30 entry window is over.
brain_help.atr: ATR = average true range of the last 14 five-minute bars: how far NQ normally moves in one bar right now.
brain_help.depth: How far price went beyond the swept level, in ATR. LIT needs at least 0.5 ATR: a real stop run, not a touch.
brain_help.idm: Inducement: a minor swing low (for a long) above the swept level, taken out on the way down before the sweep.
brain_help.disp: Displacement: the biggest candle body between the sweep extreme and the trigger, in ATR. LIT needs 0.8.
brain_help.window: Entries only between 02:00 and 15:30 ET (the entry bar's time).
brain_help.stop: Stop 1 tick beyond the sweep extreme (the protected low / high). LIT trades only 8-80 point stops.
brain_help.target: Target: the 18:00 open +/- one VIX one-day move (the VIX band). It must be at least 1.5R away; banked at 8R.
brain_help.monday: Monday rule: once Monday took Friday's high, only shorts; once it took Friday's low, only longs.
brain_help.day: One trade a day: once a setup filled, later setups that day are skipped.
brain_help.be: Breakeven: at +1R the stop moves to the entry + 1.25 pts (covers the commission and a tick).
brain_help.t_check: 15-minute check: 15 minutes after the fill, if the trade never reached +0.5R and closes more than 0.3R below the entry, it is cut at the next 1-minute open.
brain_help.two_week: Two-week eval sizing: 'one winner passes' - micros so the target pays what is left to +$3,000, capped at 60% of the room to the trailing floor, the $1,000 soft daily loss and 40 micros.
brain_help.wk_stop: Weekly stop: after 2 stop-outs in a calendar week, half size for the rest of that week (not used in two_week mode).
brain_help.vix: VIX one-day move = VIX / 100 / sqrt(252) x the 18:00 open: the market's own expected daily range.

calendar.how: Each account follows its study curve from the month it is bought: month 1 = the fee, months 2-3 = the rest of the 6-month average, months 4+ = the months 4-6 rate (net of every fee, re-buys included). Expected = Jul-Oct 2026 trades (H2, quote it); downside = the same rules on 2021-25 trades, where every mix loses its fees. Ladder (lit-funded-combo.md): Builder 50K, LucidPro, FundedNext, then 2nd and 3rd LucidPro and a 2nd FundedNext, each bought when cash (budget + payouts) allows, one a month at most.
calendar.warn: Same LIT signals on every account (81-91% correlated): more accounts = more money and the same bad months. Several accounts on one PC bot: engine/multi_account.py, OFF by default (switch on after a Sim check).
